newsitem.title: JAPAN: ALPINE SKIING-GRUENIGEN WINS SHIGA KOGEN GIANT SLALOM.
newsitem.headline: ALPINE SKIING-GRUENIGEN WINS SHIGA KOGEN GIANT SLALOM.

text.p: Swiss Michael von Gruenigen won a mens Alpine skiing World Cup giant slalom on Saturday in a combined two-run time of 2 minutes 41.68 seconds, according to unofficial results. Andreas Schifferer was second in 2:42.04 and Paul Accola third in 2:42.29.

Von Gruenigen clinched the World Cup giant slalom title by winning a mens giant slalom, the second last of the season, on a sunny morning at the Mount Higashidate course, 60 km (40 miles) northeast of Nagano in the central Japan Alps.
Gruenigen was closely followed by strong technician Schifferer of Austria, who finished 0.36 seconds slower than the 27-year old Swiss on the tough 1,487-metre course.
Saturday's victory was the reigning giant slalom world champion's third win of the season and ninth victory of his career, all in the giant slalom event.

Italian crowd-pleaser Alberto Tomba failed to qualify for the second run, finishing 35th in the first leg, but was cheered for loudest among the foreign skiiers by a mainly Japanese crowd assembled on Mount Higashidate.
